_comment: Show-level config plus the episode list. Episode `id` is the mp3 filename AND the permanent RSS guid — never rename a published episode. `order` sets play order in the feed. See AUDIO_SCRIPT_AUTHORING.md.

show.title: Morning Recall
show.description: Narrated system design and technology decisions, derived from the morning-recall prep guides. Personal study notes, read aloud.
show.author: Jaspreet Singh

episodes.title: Ticketmaster, part one — the inverse of a scale problem
episodes.summary: Why a stadium onsale is a contention problem, not a scale problem: sixty thousand total sales, a hundred and sixty-six people per seat, and the numbers done at three levels.

episodes.title: Ticketmaster, part two — two paths that barely touch
episodes.summary: The interface decisions worth narrating, the cache expiry that absorbs five million queries a second, and the purchase path end to end.

episodes.title: Ticketmaster, part three — the hold, and concurrency at a hundred and sixty-six to one
episodes.summary: Three wrong ways to expire a hold, why lazy expiration beats all of them, and the one SQL clause that turns a serialization bottleneck into parallel work.

episodes.title: Ticketmaster, part four — the waiting room, and why first-come-first-served is not fair
episodes.summary: Admission control instead of capacity, where the position counter actually breaks, and the fairness argument almost nobody raises.

episodes.title: Ticketmaster, part five — optimistic hints, the payment saga, and bots
episodes.summary: Why staleness is a feature, why compensation is asymmetric, and why the challenge belongs at queue entry rather than at purchase.

episodes.title: Ticketmaster, part six — the deliberate hot shard, and a queue allowed to lose data
episodes.summary: Sharding for isolation rather than throughput, and why a queue built on lossy infrastructure still cannot cause a double sale.

episodes.title: Figma — why not O.T., and what last-write-wins costs
episodes.summary: Why Operational Transformation is the wrong machinery for a map of objects, and the three costs of last-writer-wins with a central ordering authority.

episodes.title: Correctness under concurrency — the invariant, the fencing token, and write skew
Push notifications — the hint, not the truth
Estimation — the four-line model, and the conclusion the numbers force
Discord, part one — ingest is trivial, fanout is not
episodes.summary: Why the message write rate is the number that misleads people, and why durable per-recipient queues are actively wrong when the recipients are already connected.

episodes.title: Discord, part two — two surfaces, and three flows that each end in failure
episodes.summary: Why sends stay on HTTP, why permission checks live on the write path, and why nothing happens promptly when a session dies.

episodes.title: Discord, part three — reconnect is the real load, and why the feed answer is wrong
episodes.summary: Connections are cheap and reconnects are not, plus the node-batching that turns fifty thousand deliveries into five hundred messages.

episodes.title: Discord, part four — presence nobody scopes, and the biggest table in the product
episodes.summary: One bit flipping becomes forty thousand delivery events, and why a stale presence is invisible while a presence storm is not.

episodes.title: Discord, part five — a migration about pauses, and no broker in the delivery path
episodes.summary: Why the access pattern picks the store, why the time bucket must be coarse, and why the right component here is no component.

episodes.title: Cursor Tab, part one — the latency budget that destroys retrieval
episodes.summary: Why two hundred milliseconds forbids a retrieval pipeline, why there is no correctness invariant, and why over eighty percent of inference is wasted by design.

episodes.title: Cursor Tab, part two — retrieval without a retriever, and a codebase you do not own
episodes.summary: Ranking local editor signals in ten milliseconds, why embedding search is the last resort, and why Merkle sync is not on the Tab path at all.

episodes.title: Cursor Tab, part three — the small model is better, and cancellation must reach the accelerator
episodes.summary: Continuous batching, prefix caching, and the plumbing detail worth more than all the serving tricks combined.

episodes.title: Cursor Tab, part four — measuring a product with no correct answer
episodes.summary: Why acceptance rate is gameable, how the training flywheel narrows toward its own habits, and why nothing on the completion path is a database.
